headline: SEBI Proposes Mandatory AML Certification and Considers Two-Year Demat Dormancy Rule
summary: SEBI proposed that intermediary principal officers obtain mandatory anti-money laundering certification within six months and weighed a two-year dormancy rule for demat accounts to align treatment with trading accounts and curb misuse.
why: The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) is India's primary market regulator, and compliance mandates affect brokers, depositories, and market participants.

impacts.name: India
impacts.why: Regulatory compliance changes impact depository account management and intermediary operations.
